page: Amazon Web Services r5a.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a 2.5 GHz AMD EPYC 7571 processor delivering 64 vCPUs across 32 dedicated physical cores, using symmetric multithreading with 2 threads per core on an x86_64 architecture. The system provides 512.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Networking throughput features a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps. The instance does not include integrated local instance storage or attached GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark results highlight a notable divergence between single-threaded execution and parallel throughput. In single-core tests, the r5a.16xlarge registers poor performance, placing in the bottom 10% on Geekbench single-core (727.0), stress-ng single-core (591.0), and single-threaded gzip compression (16.7 GB/sec). Conversely, aggregate multi-threaded capabilities fall comfortably within the middle 50% across most metrics, including a PassMark CPU score of 36,739.89 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 7,518.0. Cryptographic throughput represents a particular strength, achieving a top 25% result on the PassMark CPU encryption test at 51,705.04 due to hardware AES support.

Memory performance aligns with the average band, yielding 109.01 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 52.08 GB/sec uncached write bandwidth for large blocks. In-memory operations achieve solid throughput, evidenced by 36.6 million Redis SET operations per second and a PassMark database score of 14,867.61. For machine learning inference, prompt processing reaches 884.64 tokens/sec on smaller 135M models, but drops to poor tier performance for larger 7B text generation (5.17 tokens/sec) and 70B prompt processing (4.22 tokens/sec).

With its 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the r5a.16xlarge offers cost-effective memory capacity where high core counts and massive RAM are needed without requiring top-tier single-core CPU speeds. Tradeoffs include low per-thread processing speeds and reliance entirely on network-attached storage. The instance fits large in-memory caching layers, medium-scale relational databases, big data analytics, and memory-intensive distributed enterprise applications.
description: Amazon Web Services r5a.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 64 vCPUs across 32 physical AMD EPYC 7571 cores at 2.5 GHz and 512.0 GB of DDR4 memory. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it provides 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without local instance storage or GPUs. Benchmark evaluation displays lower-tier single-thread performance alongside solid multi-core capacity, highlighted by a PassMark CPU score of 36,739.89 and strong cryptographic throughput of 51,705.04. Memory bandwidth metrics sit firmly in the middle tier, supporting 36.6 million Redis SET operations per second. While unsuited for compute-bound single-threaded tasks or large-scale LLM generation, its 1:8 core-to-memory configuration delivers high RAM density for in-memory databases, caching grids, distributed data analytics, and enterprise memory-heavy applications.
